summary: Analysis of 14 days of Nightscout telemetry (3,995 CGM readings, 98.7% coverage) indicates strong overall glycemic control with an average glucose of 121.6 mg/dL and 86.0% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL). However, safety concerns exist regarding hypoglycemia (5.1% Time Below Range <70 mg/dL), particularly overnight between 23:00 and 04:00 local time (up to 18.5% TBR at 01:00) and during the evening around 19:00 local time (15.3% TBR). The system operates with zero logged carbohydrates, relying entirely on Unannounced Meal (UAM) handling and automated Super Micro Boluses (SMBs). In combination with GLP-1 co-therapy (1.25 mg doses) and a 10-hour DIA, highly permissive automation safety limits (max IOB 25 U, max basal 12 U/h relative to ~19.7 U/day average TDD) allow late insulin stacking that drives evening crashes. A tight 90 mg/dL overnight target exacerbates nocturnal hypoglycemia. Addressing safety limits and raising the overnight target are the top safe optimization priorities.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM data coverage is excellent at 98.7% over 14 days with only 10 minor gaps (largest 65 min). 2,315 total treatments were logged, including 655 insulin entries yielding 275.95 U. Zero carbohydrate entries were logged across the period.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid CGM entries out of 4,046 expected; total_carbs_g = 0.0 across 14 days.
data_gaps: Lack of explicit meal carbohydrate amounts, meal start times, and meal composition logs.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic control is strong overall (86.0% TIR, mean 121.6 mg/dL), but Time Below Range is elevated at 5.1% (exceeding the 4.0% safety threshold). Hypoglycemia clusters overnight (00:00-04:00 local, peak 18.5% TBR at 01:00) and in the evening (19:00 local, 15.3% TBR). Severe low extremes reached 41-42 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: Glucose summary: average 121.6 mg/dL, SD 39.7 mg/dL, CV 32.6%, TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%. Extremes include 41 mg/dL on Aug 14 at 18:09 UTC and 42 mg/dL on Aug 13 at 17:09 UTC and Aug 21 at 06:19 UTC.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rate (0.6 U/h) combined with an aggressive overnight target of 90 mg/dL maintains low average glucose (90.6-106.0 mg/dL) but drives excessive nocturnal hypoglycemia. Afternoon glucose peaks around 15:00-16:00 local time (mean 162.8 mg/dL, 32.1% TAR) before crashing steeply into 19:00 (TBR 15.3%).
analysis_steps.evidence: Local hourly glucose: 01:00 local avg 90.6 mg/dL (18.5% TBR); 16:00 local avg 162.8 mg/dL (32.1% TAR); 19:00 local avg 105.4 mg/dL (15.3% TBR). Target set to 90 mg/dL from 23:00 to 08:00.
data_gaps: Inability to fully isolate true fasting basal baseline due to potential unannounced late-evening food intake.

analysis_steps.findings: ISF is flat at 56 mg/dL/U modified dynamically by oref1. DIA is set to 10 hours. Concurrent GLP-1 therapy (1.25 mg) slows gastric absorption, causing delayed glucose rises that interact with late insulin action from accumulated SMBs.
analysis_steps.evidence: Profile DIA = 10.0 h; ISF = 56 mg/dL/U flat; GLP-1 1.25 mg notes logged on Aug 14, 17, and 20.
data_gaps: Direct CR validation is blocked by zero carb entries in telemetry.

analysis_steps.findings: AAPS relies entirely on UAM and SMB delivery because carbs are not logged. UAM effectively catches delayed meal rises, but peak SMB delivery occurs hours after meals start, creating heavy tail IOB right as GLP-1 carb absorption subsides.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_always_enabled=true. Loop logs confirm frequent UAM SMB activations (e.g., Aug 19 at 15:54 UTC: UAM High Boost enacted, SMB 1.6 U, IOB 4.73 U).

analysis_steps.findings: Automation safety limits are severely elevated relative to daily requirements. Average TDD is ~19.7 U/day, yet max IOB is set to 25 U (>125% of TDD) and max basal is set to 12 U/h (15x peak scheduled basal). This allows unsafe insulin accumulation during unannounced meal spikes.
analysis_steps.evidence: max_iob_units = 25 U, max_basal_u_per_hour = 12 U/h, total insulin across 14 days = 275.95 U (avg 19.7 U/day), max scheduled basal = 0.8 U/h.

analysis_steps.findings: Observed execution is 100% reactive unannounced meal handling via automated SMBs and temp basals, with occasional manual correction boluses. No upfront prebolusing occurs. This reactive pattern causes early postprandial spikes followed by late lows.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_treatment_entries = []; representative treatments show periodic manual correction boluses (e.g., 1.1 U on Aug 14 at 16:30 UTC; 2.4 U on Aug 15 at 11:25 UTC).
data_gaps: Lack of meal start timestamps and carb entries prevents direct assessment of prebolus execution.

analysis_steps.findings: GLP-1 therapy slows absorption, stretching carb impact over 3 to 5 hours. Without e-carb entries or upfront boluses, the loop delivers reactive SMBs during late postprandial hours, stacking insulin on top of a 10-hour DIA.
analysis_steps.evidence: GLP-1 notes present; hourly glucose peaks at 16:00 local (32.1% TAR) and plunges at 19:00 local (15.3% TBR).
data_gaps: No e-carb logs present in telemetry.

analysis_steps.findings: Prioritized safe optimization plan: First, correct dangerous automation safety limits (max IOB and max basal rate) to prevent runaway insulin stacking. Second, raise the overnight target from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL to address nocturnal hypoglycemia (18.5% TBR at 01:00). Third, encourage carb logging or e-carb entries (3-4 h duration) to account for GLP-1 delayed absorption rather than relying solely on reactive UAM SMBs.
analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesis of safety limits, target segments, hourly local glucose distributions, and GLP-1 notes.

strengths: High CGM data completeness and continuity over 14 days (98.7% coverage, minimal gaps).
Strong overall Time in Range of 86.0% with an average glucose of 121.6 mg/dL.
Low overall Time Above Range (8.9% >180 mg/dL), demonstrating effective hyper-glycemic suppression.
Consistent logging of site changes, sensor changes, and GLP-1 medication administrations.
issues: Elevated overall Time Below Range at 5.1%, exceeding the clinical safety threshold of 4.0%.
Recurrent nocturnal hypoglycemia between 23:00 and 04:00 local time (peaking at 18.5% TBR at 01:00 local).
Steep late-afternoon/evening hypoglycemia around 19:00 local time (15.3% TBR).
Excessively high AAPS max IOB limit (25 U, >125% of average daily insulin requirement) and max basal limit (12 U/h, 15x max scheduled basal).
Complete absence of logged meal carbohydrates, forcing total reliance on reactive UAM SMB delivery that stacks behind GLP-1 delayed absorption.

recommendations.title: Tighten AAPS Max IOB and Max Basal Safety Limits
recommendations.description: The current max IOB of 25 U exceeds the user's total daily insulin dose (~19.7 U/day), removing vital protection against insulin stacking. The max basal rate of 12 U/h is 15 times the maximum scheduled basal (0.8 U/h). Reducing max IOB to 5-7 U and max basal to ~3.2 U/h (4x peak scheduled basal) restores critical algorithmic guardrails without constraining normal microbolusing.

recommendations.title: Raise Overnight Target to Reduce Nocturnal Hypoglycemia
recommendations.description: Target glucose is currently set to 90 mg/dL from 23:00 to 08:00. This low target contributes to significant overnight hypoglycemia (18.5% TBR at 01:00 local time). Raising the overnight target to 100 mg/dL creates a safer buffer against nocturnal lows.

recommendations.title: Introduce Meal Carbohydrate or e-Carb Logging
recommendations.description: Zero carbohydrates are currently recorded in Nightscout, forcing AAPS to handle all food via Unannounced Meal (UAM) SMBs. Under GLP-1 co-therapy, delayed gastric absorption causes UAM to deliver heavy SMBs late in the digestive process, causing late postprandial crashes at 19:00 local time. Entering carbs or using e-carbs (3-4 hour duration) provides upfront expectation of absorption without aggressive SMB stacking.

suggested_change.meal_logging_practice: Log meal carbs or use e-carbs with 3-4 hour absorption window

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise target glucose from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL between 23:00 and 08:00 to eliminate nocturnal hypoglycemia, while keeping basal rates unchanged until target effects are evaluated.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight Time Below Range reaches 18.5% at 01:00 local time with average glucose around 90 mg/dL. An overnight target of 90 mg/dL leaves no safety margin for minor night-to-night sensitivity shifts.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight glucose for 5-7 days after updating target to confirm TBR drops below 4.0% between 23:00 and 06:00.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Max IOB of 25 U is dangerously high for a total daily dose of ~19.7 U/day, enabling extreme IOB accumulation during delayed meal absorption. Max basal of 12 U/h is 15x peak scheduled basal. Reduce max IOB to 7 U and max basal to 3.2 U/h (4x peak scheduled basal) for safety.
Dynamic ISF at 70% appropriately scales ISF during hyperglycemic peaks. Retain while capping maximum allowed IOB.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Currently, 100% of meals are unannounced (0% prebolus, 0% upfront bolus) relying entirely on reactive UAM SMBs. Under GLP-1 co-therapy, transition to logging meal carbohydrates with a 10-15 minute prebolus or entering extended carbohydrates (e-carbs over 3-4 hours) to prevent reactive afternoon SMB stacking and subsequent evening crashes.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: GLP-1 slows gastric absorption, causing delayed glucose peaks at 15:00-16:00 local time. Without logged carbs or e-carbs, AAPS delivers heavy SMBs late in the meal window, causing severe hypoglycemia at 19:00 local time (15.3% TBR).
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log meal carbohydrates and start times for 5 consecutive days to observe postprandial glucose curves and assess CR accuracy.

exceptions.rationale: Reduces peak hyperglycemia at 16:00 (32.1% TAR) and prevents aggressive UAM SMB stacking that leads to the 19:00 low (15.3% TBR).

implementation_steps: Step 1: Review and update AAPS safety limits in Preferences/Config: reduce Max IOB from 25 U to 7 U, and reduce Max Basal Rate from 12 U/h to 3.2 U/h.
Step 2: Update the active profile target segments from 23:00 to 08:00, raising the target from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL.
Step 3: Monitor glucose continuously for 5-7 days to verify that overnight hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) decreases below 4.0% Time Below Range.
Step 4: Begin logging carbohydrate entries or e-carbs (3-4 hour duration) for main meals to smooth GLP-1 delayed absorption, reducing reactive SMB stacking.
education: Unannounced Meal (UAM) algorithms infer carbohydrate absorption from rising blood glucose. When GLP-1 receptor agonists delay stomach emptying, glucose rises later and more slowly, causing UAM algorithms to deliver insulin micro-doses long after the meal started.

Setting Max IOB to a value higher than total daily insulin requirements removes algorithmic guardrails, allowing closed-loop systems to build excessive insulin tails during prolonged unannounced meal absorption.

Overnight targets set close to the normal physiological lower bound (e.g., 90 mg/dL) leave very narrow margins for minor night-to-night variance in insulin sensitivity, significantly increasing time spent in hypoglycemia.
safety_notes: This analysis is for decision-support and educational review only. All proposed configuration changes must be independently reviewed and verified by the user and healthcare team.
Make profile and setting adjustments one at a time, allowing at least 3-5 days between changes to observe effects clearly.
Ensure fast-acting carbohydrates are readily available at all times, especially overnight, while evaluating target and automation limit adjustments.
